Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the piecewise linear for $x\in [-1,2]$ and the piecewise linear for $x\in [2,5].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,2].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1.5+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,5].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-3.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}-3 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
